questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words(not including the sentence given).
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument. In a world where people come from diverse backgrounds, disagreements are inevitable; yet how we handle them reveals our maturity. Rather than shouting others down or stubbornly clinging to our own views, seeking common ground through calm reasoning is always the wiser choice.

The reason is simple: friendly discussion invites cooperation, while quarrels only deepen the divide. Take the famous debates in scientific communities. When Darwin proposed his theory of evolution, opponents raised sharp objections, but progress was made not by insults but by patient argument and shared evidence. Similarly, in my own study group, a heated dispute over a project was resolved only after we sat down, listened to one another, and combined our ideas. Mutual respect turned rivals into partners.

In conclusion, differing opinions need not lead to conflict. If we approach them with an open mind, sound logic, and genuine respect, we can transform disagreement into understanding and reach a consensus that benefits everyone. This is not only a skill but a mark of a civilized society.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: M: Have you decided what you wish to study?
transcript.zh: M: 你决定想学什么了吗？

transcript.text: W: Yes, professor. I wish to study architecture.
transcript.zh: W: 是的，教授。我想学习建筑学。

transcript.text: M: Ah, that's a wonderful profession. Why did you choose it?
transcript.zh: M: 啊，那是一门很棒的职业。你为什么选择它？

transcript.text: W: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me. In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
transcript.zh: W: 我认真思考了您在上次讨论中说的话，最后决定建筑学对我来说最合适。尤其是，我很喜欢设计与工程的结合。

transcript.text: M: That's great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics. You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
transcript.zh: M: 这很好，不过我记得你之前一直在担心那些高深的数学。你现在不再觉得这方面对你来说太难了吗？

transcript.text: W: No. I was doing some online research and I think I should be able to manage. Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required. I'm certain the fruits of my labor will pay off.
transcript.zh: W: 不会。我做了一些网上调查，我觉得自己应该能够应付。数学可能是我在课程中遇到的最难的科目，但我会投入所需的努力。我相信我的劳动成果一定会得到回报。

transcript.text: M: I'm sure that's true. Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you will be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city. And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
transcript.zh: M: 我相信确实如此。由于建筑具有实体性，在这个领域，你将能够清楚地看到自己为一座城市所作出的贡献。而且你所建造的遗产将比我们这些凡人中的任何一个存在得都久远。

transcript.text: W: Yeah, I guess that's true too. So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation? I have the whole summer.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，我想这也是真的。那么，为了做准备，您觉得我应该先复习哪些科目？我整个夏天都有时间。

transcript.text: M: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree. Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics. Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
transcript.zh: M: 如今，建筑学是一门非常多样且充满活力的学位专业。大多数大学都会鼓励你学习来自哲学、经济学等广泛领域的不同知识。不过，我建议你先从计算机科学开始，因为作为项目的一部分，你将需要制作许多复杂的视觉图像。

transcript.text: W: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
transcript.zh: W: 您觉得我应该先从哪种软件开始，具体来说？

transcript.text: M: Photoshop is a good place. If you aren't yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it. And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art.
transcript.zh: M: Photoshop 是个不错的起点。如果你还不熟悉它，就尽量熟练掌握。另外，我建议你尽可能多学习的一项内容是美术，尤其是西方艺术史。

questions.stem: Why does the woman wish to study architecture?

options.text: She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings.
She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect.
She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture.
She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.信号：被问者直接应答动机 。教授先问 Why did you choose it?，她的回答里用 I'm attracted to 直接给出动机，且以 In particular 加重强调——"问因 + 被问者亲口应答 +…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确有 I'm attracted to，A 项 She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings. 借用了 attracted 这个原词，但她被吸引的是"设计与工程的结合"，不是"现代建筑的美"——美这一点录音从未说，属听到 attracted 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：preoccupied 一词录音里出现在教授口中 you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics，指她曾为数学发愁，根本不是"痴迷当建筑师的梦想"。B 项 She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect. 盗了 preoccupied 又改了对象，与问"动机"无关。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 项 She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture. 牵出一个"教建筑的父亲"，但整段录音从未提到她父亲，更没说受其影响——是预读时就警惕的"凭空多出一个人物"的诱选。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the marriage of design and engineering ↔ its integration of design and engineering marriage=integration同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: In particular, I'm attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.

questions.stem: How does the woman say she will overcome the difficulty in learning mathematics?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required.信号：转折 but 后才是真应对 。她先承认 Math might be the toughest subject，紧接 but I'll simply put in the work required——转折词 but …

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：对话里确有 professor 这个人，B 项 With the professor's help. 借"现场有教授"诱你选，但她讲克服数学的办法时只字未提靠教授，靠的是自己出力——属"同场有这人就误以为靠他"的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音里 I was doing some online research 确实出现 online，C 项 By studying the subject online. 盗了 online。但她上网只是"做了点调研"判断自己应付得来，并非"靠网上学数学"来克服难点——原词在、用途被偷换。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 项 By taking prerequisite courses. 说靠"修先修课"克服，但录音从未提到 prerequisite 或先修课程这回事——是凭空安上的办法。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（put in the work required ↔ Through hard work put in work=hard work同义概括）

questions.evidenceText: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I'll simply put in the work required.

questions.stem: What does the man say about architects' contribution to a city?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.信号：男士对城市贡献的直接断言 。男士谈到 the contribution you make to a city 后，紧接断言 the legacies you build will last much longer——…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：A 项 It is groundbreaking."具开创性"在录音里毫无对应——男士谈的是贡献能"长久存续"，不是"开天辟地"，属凭空贴标签。
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：录音里 Due to its material nature 出现 material（实体的），C 项 It is immaterial. 恰好取了它的反义 immaterial（非物质/无关紧要）。建筑明明是"实体"，选项却说"无形"，是"盗原词又反极性"的诱选。 借用原文：will last much longer than any of us mortals
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音 longer than any of us mortals 用 mortals（凡人）作对比，D 项 It is immortal. 盗这个词根改成 immortal（不朽）。原文只说贡献"比凡人活得久"，是相对的"更久"，并非"永不灭"——把相对的久夸成绝对不朽，程度过头。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（will last much longer than any of us mortals ↔ It is long-lasting last much longer=long-lasting同义）

questions.evidenceText: And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.

questions.stem: What subject does the man suggest the woman start with?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.信号：Nevertheless 转折 + suggest start with 。前句先泛举 philosophy and economics 等领域，再用 Nevertheless 一转，紧跟 I would sugge…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：philosophy and economics 里 economics 被念到，但那是男士泛举"大学会鼓励你学的各类领域"，A 项 Economics. 盗这个原词冒充答案；题问的是 start with（先学），经济学并非他建议起步的那门。 借用原文：fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 项 Philosophy. 同样来自 philosophy and economics 的泛举，philosophy 被念到却不是"建议先学"的那门——与 A 一样是"听到学科名就想划"的原词诱选。 借用原文：another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art
optionAnalysis.D: 答非所问：录音末尾 the history of Western art 确出现"西方艺术"，D 项 Western art. 盗了它。但那是男士另起一句"还建议你尽量多学美术"，与本题问的 start with（最先入手）不是同一件事——位置和性质都对不上。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I would suggest you start with computer science ↔ Computer science 原句点名即选项学科）

questions.evidenceText: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.

transcript.text: W: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet, I can't stress this enough.
transcript.zh: W: 正如我在电话里提到的，我们正在寻找一个非常谨慎低调的人，这一点再怎么强调都不为过。

transcript.text: M: I fully understand.
transcript.zh: M: 我完全明白。

transcript.text: W: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.
transcript.zh: W: 众所周知，桑切斯先生是皇家马德里非常著名的足球运动员，公众关注度很高。这意味着他出门时不可能不被认出来，也不可能不受到骚扰。

transcript.text: M: Yes, I completely understand how imperative it would be to respect Mr. Sanchez's private life.
transcript.zh: M: 是的，我完全明白尊重桑切斯先生的私人生活有多么重要。

transcript.text: W: Good. As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office. So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous. Nothing could be further from the truth. I'm telling you this so that you don't get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you.
transcript.zh: W: 很好。作为他的私人助理，你需要替桑切斯先生处理日常琐事，也就是那些由于他的名气而无法亲自去做的事情，比如去超市或邮局。所以，乍一看，为名人工作似乎很光鲜。但事实远非如此。我告诉你这些，是为了让你不要对这份工作能给你带来什么抱有不切实际的期待。

transcript.text: M: Thanks. I understand this too. This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience. I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.
transcript.zh: M: 谢谢。我对此也很清楚。这是我大学毕业后的第一份工作。所以坦白说，我之前没有多少工作经验。不过，我非常期待有机会加入这家公司，也很愿意从基层做起，无论在哪个岗位上，只要我能发挥作用就行。

transcript.text: W: That's good to hear. You sound very energetic. Tell me why you think you are well suited for this job?
transcript.zh: W: 听你这么说很好。你听起来精力很充沛。告诉我，你为什么认为自己适合这份工作？

transcript.text: M: Well, firstly, I love football. I'm a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can. I would simply love to have a job where I'm involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary. And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool. And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.
transcript.zh: M: 首先，我热爱足球。我是皇家马德里的终身支持者，只要有可能，我每个周末都会去看他们的比赛。我非常希望能找一份以某种方式参与皇家马德里事务的工作，不管职位和薪水如何。其次，我觉得这家公司在体育咨询方面所做的事情非常酷。我还认为，我的语言能力将来可能会派上很大用场。

transcript.text: W: Please tell me more about your language skills.
transcript.zh: W: 请详细说说你的语言能力。

transcript.text: M: I am fully fluent in English and Spanish and have a working proficiency in French.
transcript.zh: M: 我的英语和西班牙语都非常流利，法语也达到了工作交流水平。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about Mr. Sanchez?

options.text: He has occasionally been harassed by his fans.
He has been guarded by a discreet assistant.
He is well known to the public.
He is a famous football coach.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.信号：直接的身份介绍句 。女士用 being such a famous football player at Real Madrid 一句话给桑切斯定了身份，再用 has a very high public profi…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：He has occasionally been harassed by his fans. 借了录音 recognized and harassed 里的 harassed 一词，但录音说的是"一出门就"被骚扰、且并未限定"被粉丝"，更没说"偶尔"。题问的是"我们了解到什么"，最核心是他名气大，A把附带后果当主答案、还加了 occasionally, fans 这些原文没有的限定。 借用原文：someone who is very discreet
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：He has been guarded by a discreet assistant. 把开头 we are looking for someone who is very discreet 里的 discreet 拿来，安成"他被一位谨慎的助理护卫"。但 discreet 是对应聘者（男方）的要求，不是说桑切斯有这样一个助理——人物对应被搬错，且题问的是桑切斯本人，不是他的助理。 借用原文：famous football player
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：He is a famous football coach. 借用了录音 famous football player 里的 famous football，却把 player（球员）偷换成 coach（教练）。一字之差、身份全错，这正是预读时圈出"coach 是差异点"要防的偷换。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（has a very high public profile ↔ well known to the public 「高公众知名度」=「被公众熟知」）

questions.evidenceText: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile. This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.

questions.stem: What will the man do if he gets the job?

options.text: Play a key role in Real Madrid.
Run common daily chores for the woman.
Help promote Mr. Sanchez's public profile.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.信号：招聘者直接交代岗位 。女方用 As his personal assistant 一句明确点出岗位名，这种由招聘方直接交代"你将担任什么"的句子，就是"他将做什么"的答案句。

optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：Play a key role in Real Madrid. 借了第7、8段反复出现的 Real Madrid，把"跑腿助理"夸成"在皇马担任关键角色"。录音清楚说他要做的是 run common everyday chores（跑日常琐事），与"key role"完全相反，是过度拔高。 借用原文：run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Run common daily chores for the woman. 几乎照搬录音 run common everyday chores，只把"for Mr. Sanchez"换成"for the woman"。跑腿是为桑切斯、不是为这位招聘的女士，服务对象被掉包——正是预读时圈 for the woman 要防的张冠李戴。 借用原文：has a very high public profile
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：Help promote Mr. Sanchez's public profile. 拿了 high public profile 里的 public profile，编成"帮桑切斯提升公众形象"。但录音说的是因他名气太大、助理替他做他没法做的事（things he cannot do himself due to his fame），是"避开曝光"，绝非"提升曝光"，方向相反。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（As his personal assistant ↔ Serve as a personal assistant. 「作为私人助理」=「担任私人助理」）

questions.evidenceText: As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.

questions.stem: What does the man say about himself?

options.text: He is honest and always tells the truth.
He once worked part-time in university.
He cares little about his working hours.
He has little previous work experience.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience.信号：第一人称的自我坦白 。男方用 This is my first job after graduating from university 加 I don't have much prior working exper…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：He is honest and always tells the truth. 大概由录音里 frankly（坦白说）联想而来，但 frankly 只是说话的语气词，男方并未谈自己"诚实、总说真话"。把一个口头副词夸成性格优点，属无中生有的推断。 借用原文：after graduating from university
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：He once worked part-time in university. 用了 university 这个录音确实出现的词（after graduating from university），但男方只说"大学毕业"，从未提"在校期间打过工"。借眼熟的 university 编出一段没说过的经历，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：He cares little about his working hours. 听起来像呼应他"愿从底层做起"（keen to start from the bottom）的谦逊，但他谈的是不计职位与薪水，从没说"不在乎工作时长（working hours）"。working hours 是录音里完全没出现的话题。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I don't have much prior working experience ↔ He has little previous work experience. 「没多少经验」=「几乎没经验」）

questions.evidenceText: This is my first job after graduating from university. So frankly, I don't have much prior working experience.

questions.stem: Why does the man think he is a very competitive candidate?

options.text: He has a strong ability to connect with people.
He has a high proficiency in several languages.
He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy.
He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.信号：他自陈的优势落点 。在列举理由的段落里，男方以 I think my language skills could prove very useful 把"语言能力"点为自己的可用之长——这种"I think my ……

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：He has a strong ability to connect with people. 描述的人际沟通能力，录音通篇没有提及。他列的是爱足球、觉得公司酷、语言能力，没有任何一句谈"与人连接"，属凭"助理该会沟通"的常识脑补。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy. 盗用了录音 what this company does in sports consultancy 里的 sports consultancy。但这是他在夸"公司做的体育咨询很酷"，说的是公司的业务，不是他本人懂体育咨询——把公司的事安成了他的能力。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others. 和A一样属人际类能力，与他亲口列的"语言能力"无关，录音没说他"善于与人协作"。它和A刻意做得相像（connect with people/cooperate with others），用来分散对正确项B的注意。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（my language skills could prove very useful ↔ He has a high proficiency in several languages. 「语言能力有用」=「精通几门语言」）

questions.evidenceText: And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.

transcript.text: Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids. Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal. They don't have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
transcript.zh: 冒险运动对许多精力充沛、寻求刺激的孩子来说无疑很有吸引力。因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪和山地自行车等运动颇受欢迎。它们没有传统团队运动中那么多的规则和压力，但仍具备户外体育活动的全部益处。

transcript.text: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life. Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it's important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to. Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears. But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice. They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill-seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
transcript.zh: 在得到适当监管的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康、均衡生活的一部分。有些冒险运动可能伴随着较高的受伤风险，因此，孩子们必须弄清楚什么时候应该冒险，什么时候不应该冒险。没有任何风险的活动会剥夺孩子们挑战自我、克服恐惧的机会。但在一些人看来，正是这些风险使这类运动成为糟糕的选择。他们认为，极限运动往往会导致严重的伤害，尤其是年轻的冒险者可能会尝试对他们来说难度过高的动作。

transcript.text: But let's be real. Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not. Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children. As always, it's up to parents to decide what's best for their kids. But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives. Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
transcript.zh: 但我们还是面对现实吧。不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会做各种各样的危险事情。冒险运动也有许多相同的风险和危险，但它们还具有一种额外的冒险精神、勇气和自主意识，而这些品质对年幼的孩子来说很重要，需要加以培养。一如既往，父母应当决定什么对自己的孩子最好。但如果你确实认为冒险运动有些过于激烈，那就应该努力将其他形式的户外探险引入孩子的生活。在星空下露营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能大大帮助孩子培养与冒险运动相同的自信心和冒险精神。

transcript.text: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow. Manufacturers don't talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing. In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
transcript.zh: 今天光鲜亮丽的电子产品明天就会成为废品。当制造商宣布要推出替代你那几乎同样好用的旧产品的新款重磅产品时，他们很少提及这一点。事实上，科技公司往往故意设计使用寿命不长且无法维修的设备，以便消费者不得不花钱购买新设备。

transcript.text: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score. If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets. Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
transcript.zh: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技制造商标注可维修性评分。如果一台设备可以维修，其使用寿命就能延长，从而为消费者节省资金，并减轻大量报废电子设备给地球带来的负担。掌握了这一信息，消费者在决定购买哪些产品时就能做出更好的选择。

transcript.text: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year. This waste is dangerous. Batteries explode in recycling facilities. Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air. Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem. If they won't, governments must make them do so.
transcript.zh: 每年约有5900万吨旧电视、电脑、显示屏、智能手机、洗衣机和其他电子产品被废弃。这种废弃物是危险的。电池会在回收设施中发生爆炸。汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并散播到空气中。制造平板显示屏会向大气中排放额外的温室气体。我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。如果他们不愿意，政府就必须强制他们这样做。

transcript.text: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits. Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies. Consumers should support right-to-repair legislation. In this world, damage is a certainty. But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
transcript.zh: 尽管科技公司经常谈论环境可持续性，但许多公司却游说反对维修立法，担心这会侵蚀它们的利润。可持续性固然重要，但对这些公司而言，具有市场吸引力的设计似乎更为重要。消费者应当支持“维修权”立法。在这个世界上，损坏是必然会发生的。但我们不能任由东西坏着不管：我们制造出的问题是一个可以被解决的问题。

transcript.text: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online. This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
transcript.zh: 平均而言，美国工人每天约有10%的工作时间用于浏览互联网、给朋友发电子邮件或在线购物。这种被称为“网络闲逛”的行为，据认为每年会因生产力损失而使雇主损失高达850亿美元。

transcript.text: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies. But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time. Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction. New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
transcript.zh: 大多数关于网络闲逛的研究都集中于如何通过互联网监控和计算机使用政策等干预措施，防止员工从事这种行为。但事实证明，这类行为未必意味着员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间。研究表明，在工作中使用社交媒体与更高水平的员工敬业度和工作满意度相关。新的研究显示，网络闲逛可以帮助员工应对压力异常大的工作环境。

transcript.text: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels? That's the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study. Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations. To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping. We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they've experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at. As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit. More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection. That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn't cyberloaf as much. This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
transcript.zh: 但网络闲逛是否真的能有效降低员工的压力水平？这正是我的研究团队希望在新研究中回答的问题。我们的假设是，网络闲逛可以起到短暂休息的作用，为员工提供从压力大的工作情境中恢复的机会。为了验证这一点，我们要求员工完成一份在线调查，并对自己花在网络闲逛、查看非工作邮件和购物上的时间进行排序。我们还要求他们对工作满意度、离职意愿，以及在工作中遭受不当对待的频率进行评定，例如受到欺凌、威胁或吼叫。正如你所料，我们发现总体而言，工作中遭受的不当对待越多，工作满意度越低，离职意愿越强。更有意思的是，我们发现网络闲逛有效地缓冲了这种关联。也就是说，与网络闲逛较少的类似参与者相比，遭受不当对待但花更多时间浏览网页和查看电子邮件的员工报告了更高的工作满意度，也不太可能想要离职。这表明，网络闲逛对员工而言就像一种减压阀，帮助他们从压力经历中恢复过来。

transcript.text: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity. This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance. That isn't to say cyberloafing is always good. Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer. All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees. We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
transcript.zh: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络闲逛如何影响员工的工作表现，但我们认为，通过缓解压力，它不仅可能减少员工流失，最终还可能提高生产力。这与其他近期研究的结果相符，即进行短暂休息与更高水平的日常工作表现相关。这并不是说网络闲逛总是有益的。花费过多时间从事非工作活动很可能会导致工作表现下降。总的来说，管理者应该对员工更加宽容。我们认为，在工作中进行一些在线购物或浏览互联网，从长远来看可能会让员工更具生产力。

transcript.text: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain. That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel. But Morton was one of the world's first conservationists, stating, "For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed". So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land. By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees. A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
transcript.zh: 1854年，朱利叶斯·莫顿迁居内布拉斯加城时，面临着该地区许多定居者共同面对的问题：这里是一片没有树木的平原。这意味着没有树木可用作建筑材料，也没有木材可作燃料。但莫顿是世界上最早的自然资源保护主义者之一，他说：“为了繁荣，我们应当种植与已经耗尽和消耗掉的森林一样多的森林。”于是，他开始植树，先从自己的土地种起。到1860年，莫顿已经拥有一片由300多棵树组成的树林。几年后，他拥有的树木超过了1,000棵。

transcript.text: As the forest grew, so did Morton's influence in Nebraska. This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state's first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting. He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture. While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
transcript.zh: 随着树林不断生长，莫顿在内布拉斯加州的影响力也日益扩大。这主要是因为莫顿创办了《内布拉斯加城新闻报》，这是该州的第一份报纸；他经常在报纸上撰写社论，介绍植树在实用和审美方面的益处。他还组织成立了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并担任内布拉斯加州农业委员会委员。任职期间，莫顿想出了一个办法，要将他关于植树的信念传播到全州。

transcript.text: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves. Morton called the special event Arbor Day as "arbor" is Latin for "tree". The state government agreed. And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska. Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees. That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska—an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state. Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname "the Tree Planters State".
transcript.zh: 1872年1月4日，莫顿起草了一项决议，提议将4月10日定为内布拉斯加州植树日，并号召人们走出家门，亲自植树。莫顿把这一特别活动称为“植树节”，因为“arbor”在拉丁语中意为“树”。州政府同意了这一提议。1872年4月10日，内布拉斯加州各地庆祝了第一个非正式的植树节。植树数量最多的县、市和个人获得了奖励。那一天，内布拉斯加州种下了惊人的100万棵树，平均每位州内居民，包括男女老幼在内，种下了六棵以上的树。自1885年以来，内布拉斯加州已经种植了超过70万英亩的树木，因此获得了“植树州”的昵称。

transcript.text: Arbor Day became a legal, civic holiday in the state in 1885. It was held on April 22—Julius Morton's birthday. In addition to a parade in Nebraska City, Morton introduced what has since become a long-standing Arbor Day tradition: School children went outside and planted trees together.
transcript.zh: 1885年，植树节在该州成为法定的公民节日。节日定于4月22日举行，这一天是朱利叶斯·莫顿的生日。除了在内布拉斯加城举行游行外，莫顿还引入了一项后来成为植树节长期传统的活动：学生们走到户外，一起植树。

transcript.text: In 1970, nearly a century after Arbor Day was first celebrated, President Richard Nixon declared the last Friday of every April to be observed as National Arbor Day. All 50 states recognize the April observance, although many hold an additional state Arbor Day in a month more suited to local tree planting.
transcript.zh: 1970年，也就是植树节首次庆祝近一个世纪后，理查德·尼克松总统宣布将每年4月的最后一个星期五定为全国植树节。美国50个州都承认在4月举行的这一节日，尽管许多州还会在更适合当地植树的月份另行庆祝本州植树节。

transcript.text: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago. They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago. This is the "Out of Africa" model, as it's commonly known. In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance. But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
transcript.zh: 现代人类在大约20万年前起源于非洲。随后，他们在距今6万年后的某个时间扩散到了欧洲和亚洲。这就是人们通常所说的“走出非洲”模型。在20世纪90年代，这一假设得到了广泛接受。但鉴于过去几十年间在整个亚洲取得的一系列重要发现，这一流行观点有必要进行修改。

transcript.text: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years. This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago. Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old—a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
transcript.zh: 例如，许多新发现的人类化石（特别是在中国发现的）现在的测年结果都早于6万年前。这使人们对现代人类仅在6万年前才迁出非洲的观点提出了质疑。以最近在中国广西壮族自治区陆那洞发现的两颗现代人类牙齿为例。当我和我的研究团队对这两颗牙齿进行测年时，我们发现它们有超过7万年的历史——如果现代人类仅在6万年前才走出非洲，这种情况显然是不可能的。

transcript.text: So with such findings, what happened exactly? Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
transcript.zh: 那么，面对这些发现，究竟发生了什么？最新的数据表明我们来自何方？

transcript.text: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with? If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change. For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
transcript.zh: 我们首先应该问的问题是：现代人类最初为什么离开非洲？如果一个群体完全适应了特定环境并且拥有丰富的资源，那么确实没有理由迁移或改变。例如，非洲的一些猴子的牙齿在数百万年间几乎没有任何变化，这表明它们找到了适合自己的生存之地。

transcript.text: So what happened with humans? Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands. Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures. Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
transcript.zh: 那么人类发生了什么？一些研究人员提出，人口密度增加到了迫使较小的人类群体不得不去探索新土地的程度。另一些研究人员则认为，由于东非发生的重大环境事件，促使人类去寻找更适宜生存的环境。还有一种解释可能仅仅是，早期的现代人类猎人跟随着他们所依赖的大型动物，因此在没有意识到自己实际上正在从一个大洲迁移到另一个大洲的情况下就移出了非洲。

transcript.text: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas. This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa? No clear route across the Mediterranean from North Africa appears to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
transcript.zh: 人类每天都需要获得可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎缺乏淡水。这就带出了另一个问题：现代人类是通过哪条路线迁出非洲的？从北非穿过地中海的路线似乎并不存在明确的路径，因此早期走出非洲进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散可能是穿过了阿拉伯半岛。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: When psychologist Jessica Pryor lived near an internationally renowned university, she once saw a student walking into a library holding a sleeping bag and a coffee maker. She has heard of graduate students spending 12 to 18 hours at a time in the lab. Their schedules are meant to be literally punishing: If they are scientists-in-training, they won't allow themselves to watch Netflix until their experiments start generating results. "Relationships become estranged(疏远的)—people stop inviting them to social gatherings or dinner parties, which leads them to spend even more time in the lab," Pryor told me.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Along with other therapists, Pryor, who is now with the Family Institute at Northwestern University, is trying to sound the alarm about a tendency among young adults and college students to strive for perfection in their work—sometimes at any cost. Though it is often portrayed as a positive trait, Pryor and others say extreme perfectionism can lead to depression, anxiety, and even suicide.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: What's more, perfectionism seems to be on the rise. In a study of thousands of American, Canadian, and British college students published earlier this year, Thomas Curran of the University of Bath and Andrew Hill of York St. John University found that today's college students report higher levels of perfectionism than college students did during the 1990s or early 2000s. They measured three types of perfectionism: self-oriented, or a desire to be perfect; socially prescribed, or a desire to live up to others' expectations; and other-oriented, or holding others to unrealistic standards. From 1989 to 2016, they found, self-oriented perfectionism scores increased by 10 percent, socially prescribed scores rose by 33 percent, and other-oriented perfectionism increased by 16 percent.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: A person living with an other-oriented perfectionist might feel criticized by the perfectionist spouse for not doing household chores exactly the "right" way. "One of the most common things couples argue about is the proper way of loading the dishwasher," says Amy Bach, a psychologist in Providence, Rhode Island.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Curran describes socially prescribed perfectionism as "My self-esteem is contingent on what other people think." His study didn't examine the causal reasons for its rise, but he assumes that the rise of both standardized testing and social media might play a role. These days, LinkedIn alerts us when our rival gets a new job, and Instagram can let us know how well "liked" our lives are compared with a friend's. In an opinion piece earlier this year, Curran and Hill argue that society has also become more dog-eat-dog. "Over the last 50 years, public interest and civic responsibility have been progressively eroded," they write, "replaced by a focus on self-interest and competition in a supposedly free and open marketplace." We strive for perfection, it seems, because we feel we must in order to get ahead. Michael Brustein, a clinical psychologist in Manhattan, says when he first began practicing in 2007, he was surprised by how prevalent perfectionism was among his clients, despite how little his graduate training had focused on the phenomenon. He sees perfectionism in, among others, clients who are entrepreneurs, artists, and tech employees. "You're in New York because you're ambitious, you have this need to strive," he says. "But then your whole identity gets wrapped into a goal."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Perfectionism can, of course, be a positive force. Think of professional athletes, who train aggressively for ever-higher levels of competition. In well-adjusted perfectionism, someone who doesn't get the gold is able to forget the setback and move on. In maladaptive(不当的) perfectionism, meanwhile, people make an archive of all their failures. They revisit these archives constantly, thinking, as Pryor puts it, "I need to make myself feel terrible so I don't do this again." Then they double down, "raising the expectation bar even higher, which increases the likelihood of defeat, which makes you self-critical, so you raise the bar higher, work even harder," she says. Next comes failure, shame, and pushing yourself even harder toward even higher and more impossible goals. Meeting them becomes an "all or nothing" premise. Pryor offered this example: "Even if I'm an incredible attorney, if I don't make partner in the same pacing as one of my colleagues, clearly that means I'm a failure."

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Brustein says his perfectionist clients tend to devalue their accomplishments, so that every time a goal is achieved, the high lasts only a short time, like "a gas tank with a hole in it." If the boss says you did a great job, it's because he doesn't know anything. If the audience likes your work, that's because it's too stupid to know what good art actually is. But, therapists say, there are also different ways perfectionism manifests. Some perfectionists are always pushing themselves forward. But others actually fall behind on work, unable to complete assignments unless they are, well, perfect. Or they might handicap their performance ahead of time. They're the ones partying until 2 a.m. the night before the final, so that when the grade C rolls in, there's a ready excuse.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: While educators and parents have successfully convinced students of the need to be high performing and diligent, the experts told me, they haven't adequately prepared them for the inevitability of failure. Instead of praises like "You're so smart," parents and educators should say things like "You really stuck with it," Pryor says, to emphasize the value of perseverance over intrinsic talent. Pryor notes that many of her clients are wary she'll "turn them into some degenerate couch potato and teach them to be okay with it." Instead, she tries to help them think through the parts of their perfectionism they'd like to keep, and to lose the parts that are ruining their lives.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Bach, who sees many students from Brown University, says some of them don't even go out on weekends, let alone weekdays. She tells them, "Aim high, but get comfortable with good enough." When they don't get some award, she encourages them to remember that "one outcome is not a basis for a broad conclusion about the person's intelligence, qualifications, or potential for the future."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The treatment for perfectionism might be as simple as having patients keep logs of things they can be proud of, or having them behave imperfectly in small ways, just to see how it feels. "We might have them hang the towels crooked(不正的) or wear some clothing inside out," says Martin Antony, a professor in the department of psychology at Ryerson University in Toronto.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Brustein likes to get his perfectionist clients to create values that are important to them, then try to shift their focus to living according to those values rather than achieving specific goals. It's a play on the "You really stuck with it" message for kids. In other words, it isn't about doing a headstand in yoga class; it's about going to yoga class in the first place, because you like to be the kind of person who takes care of herself. But he warns that some people go into therapy expecting too much—an instant transformation of themselves from a pathological(病态的) perfectionist to a (still high-achieving) non-perfectionist. They try to be perfect, in other words, at no longer being perfect.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Many oppose workplace surveillance, because of the inherent dehumanizing effect it has and the relentless pressure it brings. But it's on the rise around the world as firms look to become more efficient by squeezing more productivity from their workers. More than half of companies with over $750m in annual revenue used "non-traditional" monitoring techniques on staff last year.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Monitoring employee performance gives firms the ability to assess how their staff are performing and interacting, which can be good for both the firm and employees themselves. A growing number of analytics companies offer this service. They gather "data exhaust" left by employees' email and instant messaging apps, and use name badges equipped with radio-frequency identification devices and microphones. These can check how much time you spend talking, your volume and tone of voice, even if you do not dominate conversations. While this may sound intrusive, exponents argue that it can also protect employees against bullying and sexual harassment.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Some of this data analysis can produce unexpected results. For example, it was found that people who sat at 12-person lunch tables tended to interact, share ideas more and outperform those who regularly sat at four-person tables, a fact that would probably have gone undetected without such data analysis.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Over the last few years a Stockholm co-working space called Epicenter has gone much further and holds popular "chipping parties", where people can have microchips implanted in their hands. They can use the implants to access electronically-controlled doors, or monitor how typing speed correlates with heart rate. Implanted chips may seem extreme, but it is a relatively small step from ID cards and biometrics to such devices.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: As long as such schemes are voluntary, there will probably be a growing number of convenience-oriented uses so that a substantial number of workers would opt to have a chip inserted. But if implanted chips are used to reduce slack time or rest breaks, that could prove to be detrimental. And if surveillance tools take away autonomy, that's when they prove most unpopular. A lot depends on how such monitoring initiatives are communicated and this could prevent possible revolts being staged.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: If bosses don't communicate effectively, employees assume the worst. But if they're open about the information they're collecting and what they're doing with it, research suggests 46% of employees are generally okay with it. Although many such monitoring schemes use anonymised data and participation is voluntary, many staffers remain sceptical and fear an erosion of their civil liberties.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: So workplace surveillance could be empowering for staff and useful for companies looking to become more efficient and profitable. But implemented in the wrong way, it could also become an unpopular tool of oppression that proves counterproductive.
